headline: Highest risk is medium: gpt-researcher can ingest files and browse web while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, creating moderate prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP/API calls, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content by default. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress and is a research agent, so if it consumes gpt-researcher outputs through a shared workspace or MCP path, instruction hijacking is plausible. No direct bridge is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange content through a shared file, MCP, or browser-derived artifact, prompt injection becomes actionable.
IF nuwa-skill parses gpt-researcher output as instructions without provenance checks, attacker text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted HTML/Markdown into either agent.
Add a provenance tag to every handoff artifact before B reads it.
Require a human review step for any browser-sourced content.
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for the research phase.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and images and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs, so sensitive material could leave the local environment. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, which still permits outbound transfer if it receives those artifacts. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default research workflows, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF local documents or images are passed from gpt-researcher to nuwa-skill, both agents can expose the same sensitive data class.
IF either agent forwards retrieved content to an external API, leakage extends beyond the local workspace.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of the shared research workspace.
Turn off external API calls for one run and compare outputs locally.
Redact secrets before handing artifacts between agents.
Limit outbound domains to the minimum required set.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document data-class labels and egress policy checks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher supports multiple instances and can read/write research artifacts, while nuwa-skill is runnable=false and only advertises allowlisted egress. Because B lacks documented write or concurrency capabilities, direct write-write conflict is not established. The remaining risk is limited to unusual orchestration or shared mutable state.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same writable directory or git checkout, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF nuwa-skill is wrapped in an external runner that adds write access, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Mount shared inputs read-only.
Snapshot the workspace before each run.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or transactional writes for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a planner/execution/publisher style research agent, so its outputs can become authoritative inputs for nuwa-skill if chained. nuwa-skill is a scientific-research agent and may act on those outputs without an explicit verification layer. That creates a default workflow where errors can propagate across both agents, though no downstream action authority is shown.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes gpt-researcher reports without independent source checking, hallucinations can cascade.
IF either agent is used to generate final research conclusions, upstream mistakes can be published.
mitigations: Require source citations for every claim before handoff.
Compare a sample of claims against original sources.
Insert a verification-only step between agents.
Flag uncited statements for manual review.
requires-engineering: add automated claim-checking against retrieved sources.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher explicitly handles API keys and local documents, while nuwa-skill has no documented sensitive-data classes or residency controls. The only concrete compliance concern is that A may process secrets or local documents and then send them through external APIs; B is not documented as adding a distinct residency or retention mismatch. This is a limited, single-agent compliance gap.
conditions: IF local documents contain regulated data and gpt-researcher sends them to external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator routes the same regulated dataset through both agents, policy review is required.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the run.
Use synthetic or redacted inputs.
Review API retention settings before execution.
Document the data flow for the session.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated datasets.
